calls.head: Iron sharpens iron
calls.body: The Blue Jackets are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Rangers are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Blue Jackets.
calls.call: The Blue Jackets’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Rangers.
calls.nums: Columbus 5th for chance quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · NY Rangers 5th for preventing dangerous shots

NY Rangers: a 6.1% chance of scoring on the average shot against, 5th of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 5 and 9 games this season.

calls.happened: On chance quality, Columbus had 4.9% a shot. The league average is 6.3% a shot, and they came in at 6.6% a shot.

calls.title: The Rangers won the standoff
calls.plain: The Rangers kept the Blue Jackets under the league average on chance quality.
calls.said: the Blue Jackets’ shooters would win the standoff with the Rangers’ defense

calls.head: Zibanejad gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Coyle’s line (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Bowness has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Rangers’ first line is Perreault, Zibanejad and Dorofeyev.
calls.call: The Blue Jackets’ L3 (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) spends at least 44% of its 5-on-5 time against the Rangers’ first line, against about 31% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 57% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 31% with no line matching
calls.cite: Matchups · Columbus home games this season · 4 games, 44 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 31% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Columbus’s L3 (Sillinger, Coyle, Olivier) spent 14% of its 5-on-5 time against the Rangers’ L1 (1:44 of 12:14). The call needed 44%, halfway from the 31% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 57%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier barely saw the Rangers’ first line
calls.plain: Columbus sent Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier out against the Rangers’ first line no more than they would with no line matching. Instead, Bowness sent them out against Kartye, Miller and Lafrenière (9:47 of 12:14 at 5-on-5).
calls.said: Rick Bowness would send Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier out against the Rangers’ first line again

calls.head: The Rangers’ power play has a target
calls.body: The Rangers’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Blue Jackets’ kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Blue Jackets more than most.
calls.call: The Rangers’ power play creates at least their usual 8.4 expected goals per 60.

CBJ.head: We leaned Columbus’s way (57%), and they came through.

NYR.head: We had the Rangers as slight underdogs (43%), and it went Columbus’s way.

surprises.head: Jet Greaves stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Greaves stopped all 29 shots, worth 3.7 expected goals. That is more than Columbus’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 300 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

surprises.head: Columbus shortened their bench
surprises.body: Columbus usually uses their bottom six more than most teams. Not tonight: the bottom six played 37% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 43% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

story.head: Greaves shuts out the Rangers
paras: Kent Johnson scored the only goal of the game in overtime.

The Rangers had a little more of the play, but the Blue Jackets had the finish. Jet Greaves stopped all 29 shots for the Jackets, and Dylan Garand, who gave up four goals in New Jersey in his last start, kept the Rangers in it, stopping 28 of 29. The Blue Jackets improved to 3-3-0, seventh in the Metropolitan, while the Rangers dropped to 6-3-1, second in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Kent Johnson has scored in three straight games.
Alexis Lafrenière’s six-game point streak ended.
The Blue Jackets bounced back after two straight losses.
Carson Soucy and Dmitri Voronkov were in NHL.com’s projected lineup but didn’t dress.
